link_identity.reading: the capture chain is the same one B used; this run is not a different mic or input path as far as the readback can tell

what_this_means: The 27.65 dB |H(322)| difference is not explained by a link change (pll_readback identical) and not by a microphone notch (mic is +18.8 dB there).

It is most likely an artifact of comparing a 40-line excitation against a white-noise batch: the per-bin power at 322 Hz differs by ~60 dB between the two, so any mild non-linearity in the speaker changes the ratio, and the "delay" estimated from random-phase lines is a different estimator from the one used on noise.

The 112-frame lag difference is therefore also suspect: it was measured on a random-phase multitone, not on noise. B's experiment A showed delay alone cannot inflate L1, but it did not show that a line-excited cross-correlation peak equals a noise-excited one.
decision: go back to white noise, the excitation B's protocol was built for, and normalise it to RMS -19.3 dBFS (target ref_rms = -19.3, as B confirmed). Do not tune anything else in the same step.
my_errors_to_own: I called the run white noise when it was the multitone (the patch was still active).
I compared mic/ref across two different excitation shapes (-3.64 vs -12.16 dB) as if the number were comparable. It is not.
